Thanks Vanessa — appreciate the recap. Quick answers and a few additional clarifications from legal/procurement: 

PII scope (confirmed): user_id, email address, full user messages (these frequently include account numbers and transaction references). Bank account numbers are considered sensitive and should be treated as high-risk PII.

Residency: yes — FinOptics requires EU-only residency for the pilot (inference handling and any persistent logs must remain in EU regions; no replication to the US for processing or storage).

Retention: we want raw request/response logs deleted after 90 days. Aggregated usage metrics (non-PII telemetry) may be retained up to 24 months. Any retention beyond these windows must be explicit and approved.

Training opt-out: procurement and legal require an explicit written confirmation that FinOptics data (including any material derived from it) will not be used to train, fine-tune, or benchmark Redwood models now or in the future unless FinOptics provides separate, opt-in permission. We also need confirmation that model telemetry/observability metrics will not be backfilled into public training corpora.

Also please confirm: does Redwood collect or persist any metadata that could be considered customer-identifying outside of logs (e.g., hashed user IDs, request traces)? If so, we need to understand how those are handled.

Please send the DPA redline instructions and the training opt-out text as a short standalone document so legal can include it in our procurement pack.

Hi Matt / Elena — thanks for the clear instructions. Per our internal review and after coordinating with legal and platform, please find the formal confirmations below; we’ve attached the DPA (v3) with a short training-opt-out appendix and a SOC2 summary (stub).

Formal confirmations (Redwood):
1) Training opt-out: Redwood confirms in writing that FinOptics customer data submitted to Redwood as part of the pilot (including raw request/response payloads and any derived artifacts) will NOT be used to train, fine-tune, or improve any Redwood models or training corpora now or at any point in the future unless FinOptics provides explicit, written opt-in permission. This commitment is captured in the attached "training-opt-out-confirmation.txt" and included as Appendix A in the attached DPA.

2) Data residency: For the pilot, processing and storage of persistent customer data and request/response logs will be provisioned in AWS eu-west-1. No persistent logs or model-related artifacts will be exported to non-EU regions without prior written consent.

3) Retention & deletion: Redwood will retain raw request/response logs for 90 days by default; aggregated, non-PII telemetry may be retained up to 24 months. After 90 days, raw logs will be scheduled for automatic deletion unless retention is extended by a documented, mutually agreed exception (e.g., regulatory hold).

4) Metadata / telemetry: Redwood will not backfill customer-identifying metadata or request payloads into public training corpora. System telemetry (latency, error rates, aggregate token counts) may be stored and used for internal performance diagnostics; any telemetry that contains customer identifiers will be treated as log data and subject to the 90-day retention and deletion policy above.

Next steps and deliverables:
- Attached: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf (with Appendix A: training-opt-out-confirmation.txt) and SOC2_Summary.pdf.
- Please review the DPA and return any redlines to me; we can produce an updated version within 2 business days for minor edits.
- If you want the full SOC2 report we can provide it under NDA; let me know and I’ll generate an NDA link.

If this language is acceptable, I can sign the DPA/appendix on behalf of Redwood and we’ll issue a short amendment for the pilot SOW referencing the EU residency and retention windows.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk through the appendix.
